subject: Sun and planets
title: What If the Sun Were the Size of a Basketball?

scenes.text: What if the Sun shrank to a basketball? Earth would be almost too small to see.
Earth would be a grain about two millimetres wide, sitting 26 metres away.
The Moon: a speck about six centimetres from Earth. That's as far as any human has ever gone.
Jupiter, the biggest planet, would be a grape 134 metres off.
Neptune, a small marble almost 800 metres away. Half a mile, for the edge of the planets.
And the nearest star, a tiny red dwarf, would be a ping-pong ball 6,900 kilometres away. Another continent.

description:
What if the Sun were the size of a basketball (24 cm)? Scaled down about 5.8 billion times, Earth becomes a 2 mm grain 26 metres away, with the Moon 6.6 cm from it.
Jupiter is a 2.4 cm grape 134 metres off and Neptune a marble about 780 metres away. Proxima Centauri, a red dwarf just 4.2 light-years away, would be a ping-pong ball roughly 6,900 km away.
What should we run through next?
thumbnail_text: WHAT IF THE SUN WERE A BASKETBALL?
first_comment: On this scale, a spacecraft at 17,000 mph would crawl about a millimetre every few minutes. How far away would your town be from the next star?
